title: Quadratic soft-wall transverse-vector spectrum
summary: Independent finite-difference and Chebyshev pseudospectral reproductions of the exactly solvable transverse-vector spectrum in the quadratic soft-wall AdS/QCD model.

conventions.name: metric
conventions.value: ds^2 = exp(2 A(z)) (dz^2 + eta_{mu nu} dx^mu dx^nu), A(z) = -log(z/R)
conventions.rationale: Conformally flat AdS_5 convention used by the source.

conventions.name: dilaton
conventions.rationale: Positive quadratic soft wall; the negative-sign branch has an unwanted massless vector mode.

conventions.name: units
conventions.value: hbar = c = 1; kappa in GeV, z in GeV^-1, m^2 in GeV^2
conventions.rationale: Makes the restored soft-wall scale explicit.

conventions.name: boundary conditions
conventions.value: normalizable half-line modes; numerical psi(0) = psi(z_max) = 0
conventions.rationale: The finite-domain Dirichlet problem approximates UV regularity and IR normalizability.

parameters.name: soft-wall scale
parameters.description: Positive scale controlling the radial level spacing; the benchmark default is not a phenomenological fit.

equations.description: Schrodinger form of the transverse-vector fluctuation equation.
equations.source_ref: Derived from source Eqs. (8)-(11) after restoring kappa.

equations.description: Exact squared-mass spectrum for the quadratic soft wall.
equations.source_ref: Source Eq. (15), with the soft-wall scale restored.

observables.name: vector-mode squared masses
observables.extraction: Ordered eigenvalues of the discretized one-dimensional Schrodinger operator.

acceptance_criteria: The first four numerical eigenvalues have maximum relative error below 2e-4 at the documented default resolution.
Refining the uniform grid reduces the maximum error for the first four modes with observed order between 1.8 and 2.2.

For the spectral route (refinement rule soft-wall-spectral-refinement-v2), the final maximum analytic error is below 1e-8 and either the maximum error decreases strictly across degrees N-16, N-8 and N, or every requested mode at the two finest degrees lies within its first-order perturbation scale eps ||H||_2 kappa / |lambda| with consistent eigenvector matching and cross-degree stability.

tests.expected: First four numerical squared masses reproduce 4, 8, 12, and 16 GeV^2 within tolerance.
Maximum relative error decreases at the approximately second-order rate of the centered stencil.

The spectral eigenvalues converge across degrees 24, 32, and 40 with final maximum relative error below 1e-8; at higher degrees the rounding-plateau branch of rule v2 accepts accurate, stable results while under-resolved and truncated-domain controls still fail.

claims.statement: The quadratic soft-wall vector equation has the exact spectrum m_n^2 = 4 kappa^2 (n + 1).
The HoloForge finite-difference implementation reproduces the first four exact eigenvalues within its declared tolerance.
claims.evidence: Automated analytic-spectrum and grid-refinement tests in tests/test_soft_wall_vector.py.

claims.statement: The opt-in HoloForge Chebyshev pseudospectral route reproduces the first four exact eigenvalues and passes its versioned three-degree refinement gate (rule v2).
claims.evidence: Analytic polynomial tests and spectral eigenvalue/refinement tests in tests/test_chebyshev.py and tests/test_soft_wall_vector.py.

limitations: This benchmark treats only transverse vector modes in a fixed quadratic soft-wall background.
It does not fit experimental data or validate the soft-wall model as a complete description of QCD.
The finite UV and IR numerical boundaries introduce discretization and truncation errors.
The dense spectral operator is intended for smooth low-mode verification and is not a sparse large-spectrum solver.

The rule-v2 plateau branch compares errors with a first-order perturbation scale, not a proved error floor; it was confirmed on nine reserved cases across five builds (docs/numerics/soft-wall-refinement-sa-confirmation.md).
